summary: MCP 2026-07-28 makes JSON Schema a first-class contract: Tool.inputSchema MUST be a JSON Schema object with type "object" at root; inputSchema/outputSchema/elicitation requestedSchema default to 2020-12 when $schema is absent; implementations MUST support 2020-12, MUST NOT auto-dereference network $ref, SHOULD bound composition-keyword cost, and structuredContent may be any JSON value which servers MUST make conform to outputSchema. JSON-RPC ids are string|number, never null, and must be echoed with type preserved. PowerShell's built-in cmdlets are unsuitable as the SDK's wire codec: ConvertFrom-Json (Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3/13.0.4) auto-converts ISO-date-looking strings to [DateTime] unless -DateKind String (7.5+ only), unwraps single-element arrays, emits nothing for [] or "", yields Int64/Double/BigInteger leaves, and -AsHashtable returns a case-sensitive OrderedHashtable; ConvertTo-Json defaults to -Depth 2 with silent stringification (warning only since 7.1), serializes [switch] as {"IsPresent":true}, enums as numbers, Hashtable keys in undefined order, and emits multi-line output unless -Compress. Test-Json (JsonSchema.Net 5.2.6 in 7.4.0, 7.0.4 in 7.4.13, 7.2.3 in 7.5.x, 7.4.0 in 7.6.0; drafts 6/7/2019-09/2020-12, no draft-4) installs a process-global SchemaRegistry.Global.Fetch that fetches http/https/file $ref targets — a direct MUST NOT violation — and evaluates $schema-less schemas with unspecified (union) semantics, not 2020-12. Recommended design: a PowerShell-native codec on System.Text.Json (inbox 8.0/9.0/10.0) producing ordered, case-sensitive dictionaries and a deterministic Utf8JsonWriter-based serializer; schema generation from ParameterMetadata + AST help; validation through the pwsh-bundled JsonSchema.Net via its API (not the cmdlet) with EvaluateAs=Draft202012, a throwing Fetch, and a pre-scan rejecting external $ref.

requirements.text: Support JSON Schema 2020-12 for any inputSchema/outputSchema/requestedSchema without a $schema field; validate schemas according to declared or default dialect; return an appropriate error for unsupported dialects (do not silently accept).
requirements.cite: basic/index.md: JSON Schema Usage > Implementation Requirements

requirements.text: Automatically dereference $ref values that resolve to a network URI. Any opt-in fetch mode MUST be disabled by default and SHOULD enforce allowlists/timeouts/size limits and reject loopback/link-local/private addresses. Consequence for PowerShell: Test-Json cannot be used as-is, because its BeginProcessing sets SchemaRegistry.Global.Fetch to an HttpClient/File fetcher for http/https/file URIs.
requirements.cite: basic/index.md: $ref Resolution; PowerShell TestJsonCommand.cs BeginProcessing (SchemaRegistry.Global.Fetch)

requirements.text: Reject (treat as invalid, not permissive) schemas that fail to validate because of an unresolved external $ref; apply bounds (max schema depth, max subschema count, per-validation time budget) against composition-keyword DoS.
requirements.cite: basic/index.md: $ref Resolution; Composition-Keyword Resource Use

requirements.text: Emit Tool.inputSchema as a JSON object with root type "object" (never null); for parameterless tools emit {"type":"object","additionalProperties":false} (recommended) or {"type":"object"}.
requirements.cite: server/tools.md: Data Types > Tool; schema.ts Tool.inputSchema

requirements.text: Validate all tool inputs; when outputSchema is declared, structuredContent MUST conform to it. Input validation failures are reported as tool execution errors (isError:true with actionable text), while malformed CallToolRequest / unknown tool are JSON-RPC -32602 protocol errors.
requirements.cite: server/tools.md: Output Schema; Error Handling; Security Considerations

requirements.text: When returning structuredContent, also return its serialized JSON in a TextContent block for backwards compatibility.
requirements.cite: server/tools.md: Structured Content

requirements.text: Validate structuredContent against outputSchema and validate tool results before passing to the LLM, following the $ref resolution requirements.
requirements.cite: server/tools.md: Output Schema; Security Considerations

requirements.text: On Streamable HTTP, reject (exclude from tools/list, log a warning) tool definitions whose x-mcp-header values are empty, non-tchar, contain CR/LF, are case-insensitively duplicated, sit on non-primitive or number-typed properties, or are not statically reachable through a properties-only chain (no items/oneOf/anyOf/allOf/not/if-then-else/$ref). Stdio clients MAY ignore x-mcp-header.
requirements.cite: server/tools.md: x-mcp-header; streamable-http.md: Custom Headers from Tool Parameters

requirements.text: JSON-RPC request id is string or integer, never null, and unique among outstanding requests of the sender; responders echo it with its JSON type preserved (a string id "1" must not come back as number 1).
requirements.cite: basic/index.md: Requests; schema.ts RequestId = string | number

requirements.text: Stdio messages are newline-delimited and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines; UTF-8; nothing but valid MCP messages on stdout/stdin. Therefore any serializer used for the wire must produce single-line output (ConvertTo-Json requires -Compress; Newtonsoft Formatting.Indented uses Environment.NewLine).
requirements.cite: transports/stdio.md: lines 15-22

requirements.text: Form-mode requestedSchema is a flat object whose properties are only StringSchema/NumberSchema/BooleanSchema/EnumSchema; no nesting, no arrays of objects; servers MUST NOT request secrets/credentials via form mode (use URL mode).
requirements.cite: client/elicitation.md: Requested Schema; Security Considerations; schema.ts ElicitRequestFormParams

requirements.text: Clients SHOULD validate elicitation responses against requestedSchema; servers SHOULD validate received content matches the schema; clients supporting defaults SHOULD pre-populate fields.
requirements.cite: client/elicitation.md: Security Considerations items 2-3; Requested Schema

requirements.text: SDK wire codec must not use ConvertFrom-Json for inbound messages on 7.4 (no -DateKind): Newtonsoft DateParseHandling.DateTime turns any ISO-8601-looking string value (e.g. elicitation date-time answers, tool arguments) into [DateTime], changing the JSON type on round-trip. Use System.Text.Json (JsonDocument/JsonNode/Utf8JsonReader) or Newtonsoft with DateParseHandling.None.
requirements.cite: PowerShell JsonObject.cs ConvertFromJson (JsonDateKind.Default => DateParseHandling.DateTime, RoundtripKind); ConvertFrom-Json.md 7.6 (-DateKind introduced 7.5)

requirements.text: SDK serializer must convert [switch]/SwitchParameter to JSON boolean, byte[] to base64 string for blob fields, enums to names (or explicit numeric policy), DateTime/DateTimeOffset to ISO 8601 round-trip strings, and must never rely on ConvertTo-Json's default -Depth 2 (silent stringification of deeper levels; warning only since 7.1).
requirements.cite: PowerShell JsonObject.cs ProcessValue (leaf type list, IsPrimitive, enum handling, JsonMaxDepthReached); ConvertToJsonCommand.cs (_depth = 2, ValidateRange 0-100)

requirements.text: When validating with the pwsh-bundled JsonSchema.Net API directly, set EvaluationOptions.EvaluateAs = SpecVersion.Draft202012 (or inject $schema) because with $schema absent JsonSchema.Net evaluates as SpecVersion.Unspecified (all-keywords union), not 2020-12; and install a Fetch delegate that THROWS, because a per-options registry falls back to SchemaRegistry.Global.Fetch when the local Fetch returns null (`Fetch(baseUri) ?? Global.Fetch(baseUri)`), and Global.Fetch may have been set to an HTTP fetcher by any prior Test-Json call in the process.
requirements.cite: json-everything schema-v7.2.3 SchemaRegistry.cs line 226; EvaluationOptions.cs EvaluateAs; JsonSchema.cs line 464/536; PowerShell TestJsonCommand.cs

requirements.text: Pre-scan every schema (own and remote) for $ref values that are absolute URIs with http/https (or any non-local scheme) not resolvable within the document's $id/$defs/$anchor set, and reject the tool/elicitation definition with a clear error before any validator runs; this is dialect- and library-independent enforcement of the MUST NOT.
requirements.cite: basic/index.md: $ref Resolution

requirements.text: Generate inputSchema from ParameterMetadata: [Parameter(Mandatory)] in the selected/default parameter set -> required; type map (see wire_details); [ValidateSet] -> enum; [ValidateRange] -> minimum/maximum (ValidateRangeKind.Positive -> exclusiveMinimum 0, NonNegative -> minimum 0, Negative -> exclusiveMaximum 0, NonPositive -> maximum 0); [ValidateLength] -> minLength/maxLength; [ValidateCount] -> minItems/maxItems; [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty] on string -> minLength 1, on array -> minItems 1; [ValidatePattern] -> pattern only when the .NET regex is ECMA-262-compatible (otherwise put it in description); comment-based help .PARAMETER -> property description, .SYNOPSIS (+ .DESCRIPTION) -> tool description; [Parameter(HelpMessage)] as description fallback; constant default values from the AST -> default.
requirements.cite: PowerShell platform knowledge (System.Management.Automation.ParameterMetadata, ValidateRangeAttribute, CommentHelpInfo); server/tools.md Data Types

requirements.text: Exclude common/optional common parameters ([System.Management.Automation.Cmdlet]::CommonParameters and ::OptionalCommonParameters, plus WhatIf/Confirm) and reject or hide SecureString/PSCredential/ScriptBlock/PSObject-typed parameters from generated schemas; treat multiple parameter sets by default as a flattened union (required = mandatory in all sets, sets described in description) with an opt-in oneOf mode.
requirements.cite: server/tools.md Data Types; elicitation.md Security (no secrets via form); PowerShell platform knowledge

requirements.text: Represent decoded JSON objects as insertion-ordered, case-sensitive dictionaries (System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary with StringComparer.Ordinal, or OrderedHashtable) and JSON arrays as [object[]]/List[object] that are never pipeline-unwrapped (use Write-Output -NoEnumerate or the unary comma when returning); JSON null -> $null present in the dictionary; missing key -> key absent. Use ContainsKey, not truthiness, to distinguish null from missing.
requirements.cite: PowerShell OrderedHashtable.cs (default OrderedDictionary comparer); ConvertFrom-Json.md 7.6 -AsHashtable notes

requirements.text: Offer -OutputSchema generation from [OutputType([type])] when the argument is a resolvable .NET/PowerShell class (public properties -> properties, Nullable<T> -> [T,"null"], cycle guard, depth cap); omit outputSchema when only string type names are given.
requirements.cite: server/tools.md Output Schema; PowerShell platform knowledge (OutputTypeAttribute)

requirements.text: Expose x-mcp-header through a PowerShell attribute class (e.g. [McpHeader('Region')]) or a schema-override hashtable on the tool registration; when emitting, enforce all constraints (tchar name, uniqueness, primitive integer/string/boolean only, safe-integer range) on the server side so clients never have to drop the tool.
requirements.cite: server/tools.md x-mcp-header; streamable-http.md Custom Headers from Tool Parameters

requirements.text: Use System.Text.Json.Schema.JsonSchemaExporter (System.Text.Json 9.0+, i.e. pwsh 7.5+/7.6) to derive schemas for .NET/PowerShell class types; on pwsh 7.4 (STJ 8.0) fall back to reflection-based generation.
requirements.cite: PowerShell SMA csproj TargetFramework net8.0 (7.4) / net9.0 (7.5) / net10.0 (7.6); .NET platform knowledge

wire_details: MCP constants: default dialect when $schema absent = https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema; explicit alternative shown in spec examples: "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#". Tool.inputSchema root MUST be type "object". Elicitation StringSchema.format ∈ {email, uri, date, date-time}. LegacyTitledEnumSchema key `enumNames` (non-standard). Elicitation result content values: string | number | boolean | string[]. JSON-RPC id: string | number (integer), never null. Error codes: -32602 invalid params/unknown tool; -32020..-32099 reserved for MCP; -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError. x-mcp-header -> HTTP header `Mcp-Param-{name}`; integer header values within -(2^53-1)..(2^53-1). Conformance harness validates every wire message against the spec JSON schema (check `wire-schema-valid`); scenario `json-schema-2020-12-preservation` exists but is not scored (added-after-release).

Stdio framing: one JSON-RPC message per line, no embedded newlines, UTF-8; ConvertTo-Json output MUST be produced with -Compress (Newtonsoft Formatting.Indented uses Environment.NewLine, CRLF on Windows).

Bundled libraries (from PowerShell/PowerShell csproj files): PowerShell 7.4.0 = net8.0, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, JsonSchema.Net 5.2.6; 7.4.13 = Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, JsonSchema.Net 7.0.4 (+ Json.More.Net 2.0.2, JsonPointer.Net 5.0.2) — i.e. the JsonSchema.Net MAJOR changed within the 7.4 servicing line; 7.5.0/7.5.4 = net9.0, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, JsonSchema.Net 7.2.3; 7.6.0 (and master) = net10.0, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4, JsonSchema.Net 7.4.0. System.Text.Json is inbox with the shared framework: 8.0.x (7.4), 9.0.x (7.5), 10.0.x (7.6). Assemblies live in $PSHOME (JsonSchema.Net.dll, Newtonsoft.Json.dll).

ConvertTo-Json (ConvertToJsonCommand.cs): -InputObject <Object> (pipeline; multiple inputs or -AsArray -> array), -Depth <int> default 2, [ValidateRange(0,100)]; -Compress; -EnumsAsStrings (adds Newtonsoft StringEnumConverter); -AsArray; -EscapeHandling <Newtonsoft.Json.StringEscapeHandling> Default|EscapeNonAscii|EscapeHtml. Internals: Newtonsoft JsonConvert.SerializeObject with MaxDepth=1024, StringEscapeHandling, Formatting.Indented unless -Compress. Leaf pass-through types: string, char, bool, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, Guid, Uri, double, float, decimal, BigInteger, any Type.IsPrimitive (all integer types), enums (Int64/UInt64-based enums become ToString()). NullString.Value and DBNull -> null. Beyond MaxDepth: LanguagePrimitives.ConvertTo(obj,[string]) and one warning 'Resulting JSON is truncated as serialization has exceeded the set depth of {0}.' (WebCmdletStrings.JsonMaxDepthReached, only when a Cmdlet context exists). IDictionary -> Dictionary<string,object> in enumeration order (Hashtable order undefined; OrderedDictionary/[ordered] preserved); non-string dictionary keys -> terminating error NonStringKeyInDictionary. IEnumerable -> array. Other objects -> ProcessCustomObject (public properties, honoring [JsonIgnore]) plus PSObject extended properties (AppendPsProperties), except ETS props on string/DateTime base objects are skipped (7.2+). Consequences: [switch] -> {"IsPresent":true}; [Version] -> object of Major/Minor/Build/Revision/...; [TimeSpan] -> object (Ticks, Days, ...); byte[] -> JSON array of numbers (no base64); DateTime -> ISO 8601 by Newtonsoft (Kind Unspecified => no offset, Local => +hh:mm, Utc => Z); Uri/Guid -> string.

ConvertFrom-Json (ConvertFromJsonCommand.cs): -InputObject <string> (Mandatory, pipeline; multiple pipeline strings are first tried individually, otherwise joined with Environment.NewLine), -AsHashtable, -Depth <int> default 1024 [ValidateRange(Positive)], -NoEnumerate, -DateKind <Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.JsonDateKind> Default|Local|Utc|Offset|String (7.5+). Internals (JsonObject.cs): Newtonsoft JsonConvert.DeserializeObject with TypeNameHandling.None, MetadataPropertyHandling.Ignore, MaxDepth, DateParseHandling (Default/Local/Utc => DateTime; Offset => DateTimeOffset; String => None), DateTimeZoneHandling (Default => RoundtripKind). Leaves are JValue.Value: Int64 for integers, BigInteger on Int64 overflow, Double for floats (FloatParseHandling.Double default), string, bool, null, DateTime when auto-detected. Objects -> PSObject with PSNoteProperty (property order preserved; case-insensitive duplicate keys -> terminating error KeysWithDifferentCasingInJsonString / DuplicateKeysInJsonString; empty-string key -> error) or, with -AsHashtable, System.Management.Automation.OrderedHashtable (7.3+; built on a default-comparer OrderedDictionary => CASE-SENSITIVE keys, unlike @{} / [ordered]@{} which are case-insensitive). Arrays -> object[] enumerated to the pipeline: '[1]' becomes 1, '[]' emits nothing, unless -NoEnumerate. Empty-string input emits nothing. Newtonsoft leniency: comments, single quotes, trailing commas accepted; NaN/Infinity tokens accepted.

Test-Json (TestJsonCommand.cs): parameter sets JsonString|JsonPath|JsonLiteralPath × (none|WithSchemaString|WithSchemaFile): -Json <string> (Position 0, pipeline), -Path/-LiteralPath, -Schema <string> (Position 1), -SchemaFile <string>, -Options <string[]> [ValidateSet('IgnoreComments','AllowTrailingCommas')] (present on master/7.5+; absent in v7.4.0 source). Parsing via System.Text.Json JsonNode.Parse with JsonDocumentOptions {CommentHandling Disallow unless IgnoreComments, AllowTrailingCommas}. Schema via Json.Schema.JsonSchema.FromText / FromFile. Evaluation: _jschema.Evaluate(node, new EvaluationOptions { OutputFormat = OutputFormat.Hierarchical }) on master (OutputFormat.List in 7.4.0); no EvaluateAs, no RequireFormatValidation set (=> `format` is annotation-only, email/date-time NOT validated). Output: $true/$false plus non-terminating ErrorRecords: ErrorId InvalidJsonAgainstSchemaDetailed (message = '{error.Value}' + InstanceLocation), InvalidJsonSchema, InvalidJson, JsonSchemaFileOpenFailure. BeginProcessing sets the STATIC SchemaRegistry.Global.Fetch = uri => http/https via new HttpClient().GetStringAsync(uri).Result, file:// via File.ReadAllText, other schemes throw; wrapped in JsonSchemaReferenceResolutionException. Docs (7.4 Test-Json.md NOTES): since 7.4 uses System.Text.Json + JsonSchema.NET; 'No longer supports Draft 4 schemas'; 'Only supports strictly conformant JSON'.

JsonSchema.Net 7.2.3 (bundled in 7.5.x) API facts: Json.Schema.JsonSchema.FromText(string) / FromFile(path) / JsonSerializer.Deserialize<JsonSchema>; JsonSchema.Evaluate(JsonNode, EvaluationOptions) -> EvaluationResults {IsValid, HasErrors, Errors: IReadOnlyDictionary<string,string>, HasDetails, Details, InstanceLocation, EvaluationPath, SchemaLocation}; EvaluationOptions {EvaluateAs: SpecVersion (init; Unspecified default), OutputFormat: Flag|List|Hierarchical, RequireFormatValidation (default false), OnlyKnownFormats, ValidateAgainstMetaSchema, SchemaRegistry (per-options instance), AllowReferencesIntoUnknownKeywords=true}; SpecVersion members include Draft6, Draft7, Draft201909, Draft202012, DraftNext (exact enum names to verify per version); SchemaRegistry {Global (static), Fetch: Func<Uri, IBaseDocument?>, Register(JsonSchema)}; lookup chain: local registered -> Global registered -> local Fetch -> Global.Fetch. JsonSchema.cs line 536: keyword-support check returns true for all keywords when preferredVersion == Unspecified (union semantics). In json-everything master (newer major) the Fetch signature changed to Func<Uri, SchemaRegistry, IBaseDocument?> and EvaluateAs was removed from EvaluationOptions — expect API drift across pwsh versions (5.2.6 vs 7.0.4 vs 7.2.3 vs 7.4.0).

System.Text.Json API set usable from PowerShell without compilation: [System.Text.Json.JsonDocument]::Parse(string|Stream|ReadOnlyMemory, JsonDocumentOptions); JsonElement.ValueKind (Object/Array/String/Number/True/False/Null/Undefined), .EnumerateObject()/.EnumerateArray(), .GetString(), .TryGetInt64([ref]), .TryGetDouble, .TryGetDecimal, .GetRawText(); [System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode]::Parse, JsonObject (insertion-ordered, case-sensitive by default; JsonNodeOptions.PropertyNameCaseInsensitive), JsonArray, JsonValue; Utf8JsonWriter over a MemoryStream/ArrayBufferWriter with JsonWriterOptions {Indented=$false, Encoder=[System.Text.Encodings.Web.JavaScriptEncoder]::UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping (to avoid ' etc. escaping of + < > & ' and non-ASCII), SkipValidation}; WriteStartObject/WritePropertyName/WriteStringValue/WriteNumberValue(long|double|decimal)/WriteBooleanValue/WriteNullValue/WriteBase64StringValue(byte[])/WriteRawValue(string) (6.0+). JsonSerializer.Serialize on PSObject-wrapped values serializes PSObject's public properties (BaseObject, Members, ...) — must unwrap ([System.Management.Automation.PSObject]::Base($o) / $o.psobject.BaseObject) or write your own walker. Default STJ encoder escapes non-ASCII as \uXXXX (valid JSON, larger payload). Numbers: STJ writes double via shortest round-trip ('R'-equivalent); JsonNumberHandling.AllowNamedFloatingPointLiterals needed for NaN/Infinity (which are not valid JSON anyway).

PowerShell metadata APIs for schema generation: (Get-Command X).Parameters -> Dictionary<string, System.Management.Automation.ParameterMetadata> {Name, ParameterType, IsDynamic, Aliases, Attributes, ParameterSets: Dictionary<string, ParameterSetMetadata {IsMandatory, Position, ValueFromPipeline, HelpMessage, ...}>}; CommandInfo.ParameterSets: ReadOnlyCollection<CommandParameterSetInfo> {Name, IsDefault, Parameters: CommandParameterInfo {Name, ParameterType, IsMandatory, Position, HelpMessage, Aliases, Attributes}}; attribute classes: System.Management.Automation.ParameterAttribute {Mandatory, ParameterSetName, Position, HelpMessage}, ValidateSetAttribute {ValidValues; or a ValidValuesGenerator type via ctor}, ValidateRangeAttribute {MinRange, MaxRange (object)}, ValidateRangeKind enum Positive|NonNegative|Negative|NonPositive (7.x), ValidateLengthAttribute {MinLength, MaxLength}, ValidateCountAttribute {MinLength, MaxLength}, ValidatePatternAttribute {RegexPattern, Options}, ValidateNotNullAttribute, ValidateNotNullOrEmptyAttribute, ValidateNotNullOrWhiteSpaceAttribute (7.4+), AliasAttribute {AliasNames}, PSDefaultValueAttribute {Value, Help}, ArgumentCompletionsAttribute (7.x; hint only), OutputTypeAttribute {Type: PSTypeName[]}. Defaults: (Get-Command X).ScriptBlock.Ast (FunctionDefinitionAst).Body.ParamBlock.Parameters[i].DefaultValue (ExpressionAst) -> .SafeGetValue() (throws for non-constant). Help: FunctionDefinitionAst.GetHelpContent() / ScriptBlockAst.GetHelpContent() -> System.Management.Automation.Language.CommentHelpInfo {Synopsis, Description, Parameters: IDictionary<string,string>, Notes, Examples, Outputs, Inputs}; or Get-Help -Full (slower, needs module context; .description[].Text, .parameters.parameter[].description[].Text). Common parameters: [System.Management.Automation.Cmdlet]::CommonParameters (string[]) and ::OptionalCommonParameters; also 'WhatIf','Confirm' when SupportsShouldProcess.

Recommended PowerShell type -> JSON Schema map: string,char -> {type:string} (char maxLength 1); bool, SwitchParameter -> {type:boolean}; byte,sbyte,int16,uint16,int32,uint32,int64 -> {type:integer} (+minimum 0 for unsigned; int64 outside 2^53 loses precision in JS clients — note in description); uint64,BigInteger -> {type:integer}; single,double,decimal -> {type:number}; DateTime,DateTimeOffset -> {type:string, format:date-time}; Guid -> {type:string, format:uuid}; Uri -> {type:string, format:uri}; TimeSpan -> {type:string} (document .NET 'd.hh:mm:ss.fffffff' form; not ISO 8601 duration); Version/SemanticVersion -> {type:string}; enum -> {type:string, enum:[names]} ([Flags] -> array of enum strings or comma-separated string, choose one); Nullable<T> -> {type:[T,"null"]}; T[], List<T>, IEnumerable<T> -> {type:array, items:schema(T)}; object[], ArrayList, IEnumerable -> {type:array}; Hashtable/IDictionary/OrderedDictionary -> {type:object, additionalProperties:true}; PSObject/PSCustomObject/object -> {} (any); PowerShell class / .NET POCO -> {type:object, properties from public instance properties, additionalProperties:false optional, cycle guard}; SecureString, PSCredential, ScriptBlock, FileInfo etc. -> reject/skip (not JSON-representable or secret). [ValidateSet] on string[] parameter -> {type:array, items:{type:string, enum:[...]}} (also the elicitation multi-select shape).

Elicitation form schema from PowerShell types (server side): string/Guid/Uri/DateTime(DateTimeOffset) -> StringSchema (format uri / date-time; email only via explicit metadata); integer types -> NumberSchema type integer; single/double/decimal -> NumberSchema type number; bool/switch -> BooleanSchema; enum or [ValidateSet] -> UntitledSingleSelectEnumSchema (enum: names/values) or TitledSingleSelectEnumSchema (oneOf const/title when display labels are supplied); string[]/enum[] with [ValidateSet] -> Untitled/TitledMultiSelectEnumSchema with minItems/maxItems from [ValidateCount]; [ValidateRange] -> minimum/maximum; [ValidateLength] -> minLength/maxLength; Mandatory -> required[]; constant default -> default; anything else (arrays of non-enum, nested objects, hashtables) -> refuse with a clear error. ElicitResult.content mapping back: number -> convert to declared numeric type via [LanguagePrimitives]::ConvertTo; date/date-time strings stay strings unless the tool parameter type is DateTime (then parse with [DateTimeOffset]::Parse(...,InvariantCulture, RoundtripKind)).
sdk_implications: Wire codec decision: implement `ConvertFrom-McpJson`/`ConvertTo-McpJson` (private) on System.Text.Json, not on ConvertFrom-Json/ConvertTo-Json. Reader: JsonDocument.Parse (or Utf8JsonReader) -> recursive conversion to an insertion-ordered, case-sensitive OrderedDictionary (StringComparer.Ordinal) for objects, object[] for arrays, [string]/[bool]/$null leaves, numbers as Int64 when TryGetInt64 succeeds, otherwise Double (or Decimal/raw text for out-of-range). Never let ISO date strings become DateTime. Writer: a PowerShell walker over Utf8JsonWriter (Indented=$false, UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping) that unwraps PSObject, maps SwitchParameter->bool, enum->name (policy flag), DateTime/DateTimeOffset->'o' round-trip string, Guid/Uri/Version/TimeSpan->string, byte[]->base64 only where the SDK models a blob field, IDictionary->object (string keys enforced), IEnumerable (not string)->array, PSCustomObject/class->object of properties, with an explicit max depth (e.g. 64) that ERRORS instead of truncating.

JSON-RPC id handling: model id as a small discriminated value: keep the JsonElement.ValueKind at decode (String vs Number) and store either [string] or [long] (fallback: raw text via GetRawText for non-Int64 numbers, re-emitted with Utf8JsonWriter.WriteRawValue). Outgoing ids: use Int64 counters (or GUID strings); never generate floats. Reject id null (spec MUST NOT be null) and non-unique outstanding ids on receive. Do not use ConvertFrom-Json for this: it yields Int64/BigInteger/Double and loses '1.0' vs '1' distinctions, and ConvertTo-Json re-serialises Double 1 as 1.0.

Empty-array / single-element pitfalls: every internal function that returns decoded JSON arrays must use `,$array` or Write-Output -NoEnumerate; every serializer call site must pass -InputObject or the walker must inspect the object directly (no pipeline). structuredContent may legitimately be [] or a scalar — the writer must serialize `@()` as [] and `$null` as null, and the tool result builder must distinguish 'structuredContent absent' from 'structuredContent = $null' (use ContainsKey on the result dictionary).

Schema validation strategy: (1) load the pwsh-bundled JsonSchema.Net from $PSHOME (Add-Type -Path "$PSHOME/JsonSchema.Net.dll" or [System.Reflection.Assembly]::LoadFrom; verify the assembly is already in the default ALC when Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Utility is loaded so no double-load occurs); (2) wrap `Json.Schema.JsonSchema.FromText` + `Evaluate` with EvaluationOptions { EvaluateAs = Draft202012 when no $schema, OutputFormat = List (5.2.6) / Hierarchical (7.x), RequireFormatValidation = $true for elicitation, SchemaRegistry.Fetch = { throw } }; (3) before evaluation, pre-scan for external $ref (absolute http/https/other-scheme URIs not equal to a local $id) and reject; (4) enforce resource bounds (schema depth ≤ 32, subschema count cap, evaluation timeout via CancellationToken or a size gate) per basic/index Composition-Keyword Resource Use; (5) map EvaluationResults to a list of {instancePath, keyword, message} for isError tool results. Because JsonSchema.Net's public API drifted between 5.2.6 (7.4.0), 7.0.4 (7.4.13), 7.2.3 (7.5) and 7.4.0 (7.6), write a thin adapter with version probing ([Json.Schema.JsonSchema].Assembly.GetName().Version) and a pure-PowerShell fallback validator covering the elicitation primitive subset and the common tool-input keywords (type, properties, required, additionalProperties, enum, const, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, pattern, items, minItems/maxItems, oneOf/anyOf/allOf) when the bundled library cannot be used (e.g. ConstrainedLanguage, unexpected version).

Do NOT bundle a private JsonSchema.Net/NJsonSchema/Json.More.Net/JsonPointer.Net: pwsh already loads JsonSchema.Net (+ Json.More.Net, JsonPointer.Net, System.Text.Json) into the default AssemblyLoadContext once Test-Json or Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Utility types touch it; a second version by the same simple name either fails to load or produces type identity conflicts (Json.Schema.JsonSchema from two assemblies). If a private copy is unavoidable, it must be isolated in a custom AssemblyLoadContext via a compiled C# shim (Add-Type at import, Roslyn cost ~1-2 s, unavailable in ConstrainedLanguage) — treat as last resort.

Test-Json cmdlet may be offered only as an opt-in convenience for users, never on the SDK's hot path: it (a) mutates SchemaRegistry.Global.Fetch to a network fetcher (spec MUST NOT), (b) requires the instance as a JSON string (double serialization), (c) does not enforce 2020-12 for $schema-less schemas, (d) ignores `format`, (e) reports violations only as non-terminating errors (collect via -ErrorVariable/-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue), (f) lacks -Options on 7.4.0. If the SDK ever calls Test-Json, it must afterwards reset [Json.Schema.SchemaRegistry]::Global.Fetch to a throwing delegate.

Schema generation module (`New-McpToolSchema`): input = CommandInfo (function, cmdlet, or script block with param()). Steps: pick parameter set (default set or -ParameterSet); iterate CommandParameterSetInfo.Parameters minus common parameters; for each: name (keep PowerShell casing; optional camelCase policy with a reverse map for binding), type map, constraints from attributes, description from CommentHelpInfo.Parameters (match case-insensitively; verify whether keys are upper-cased), HelpMessage fallback, default from AST SafeGetValue, `required` from IsMandatory; emit additionalProperties:false by default (rejects hallucinated args early and gives clean isError feedback), plus `$schema` omitted (2020-12 default). Tool description = Synopsis + '\n\n' + Description (trimmed). Aliases are not representable in JSON Schema; accept aliased keys at binding time only if an option is set, else reject as unknown property. Cache the generated schema per command (it is immutable per session).

Argument binding: convert the validated argument dictionary to a splat hashtable with the original parameter names; convert numbers to the declared parameter type ([LanguagePrimitives]::ConvertTo($v, $param.ParameterType)); booleans to [switch]; arrays to typed arrays; nested OrderedDictionary to [pscustomobject] or hashtable per parameter type; strings to DateTime/Guid/Uri via the .NET parsers with InvariantCulture. Never invoke the command via Invoke-Expression; use & $cmd @splat inside the SDK's runspace.

Structured output path: if the tool declares outputSchema, serialize the returned object with the SDK writer to a JSON string, parse back to JsonNode for validation, and on failure return isError:true with the validator messages (server MUST conform, so do not send non-conforming structuredContent). Always add a TextContent block with the same JSON (spec SHOULD).

Elicitation client side: implement a small validator for the primitive subset in pure PowerShell (type, enum/oneOf-const, minLength/maxLength, minimum/maximum, minItems/maxItems, format email/uri/date/date-time via [mailaddress]/[Uri]::TryCreate/[DateTimeOffset]::TryParseExact) so that ElicitResult.content is validated without JsonSchema.Net; accept LegacyTitledEnumSchema (`enumNames`) on input; render titles from oneOf/anyOf const+title. Server side: `ConvertTo-McpElicitationSchema` from a param block or a hashtable; refuse non-primitive members with an error naming the offending parameter.

x-mcp-header client behaviour on Streamable HTTP: implement the constraint checker (tchar regex '^[!#$%&''*+.^_`|~0-9A-Za-z-]+$', case-insensitive uniqueness, properties-only reachability walk, type ∈ integer|string|boolean, integer safe range) and drop violating tools from the tools/list result with Write-Warning including tool name and reason; header value extraction reads the exact properties path in arguments and omits the header when absent. On stdio, ignore.

Encoding: stdio writer must emit UTF-8 without BOM ([System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)) and '\n' line endings; do not rely on Console.Out / [Console]::OutputEncoding (Windows default may be code page); open stdout via [Console]::OpenStandardOutput() and a StreamWriter with the BOM-less encoding; reader must accept '\r\n' terminated lines tolerantly. STJ default encoder's \uXXXX escaping of non-ASCII is valid but inflates payloads; prefer UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping and let the transport carry raw UTF-8.

Performance: STJ parsing of large tool results (MBs) in PowerShell is dominated by the per-element object conversion loop, not by the parser; provide a lazy mode that keeps JsonElement/JsonNode for pass-through fields (e.g. forwarding structuredContent unchanged) and only materializes what handlers touch. Cache compiled JsonSchema objects per tool (FromText is the expensive step). Measure ConvertTo-Json vs Utf8JsonWriter walker for typical 10-100 KB payloads in the implementation phase.

Documentation obligation (spec SHOULD): the SDK docs must state supported dialects: 2020-12 (default, enforced), 2019-09, draft-07, draft-06 via the bundled JsonSchema.Net; draft-04 unsupported (return a clear 'unsupported dialect' error, mapped to -32602 for inbound schemas or a registration-time error for own tools).
legacy_delta: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (.NET Framework, System.Web.Extensions JavaScriptSerializer): no Test-Json at all (introduced 6.1); ConvertFrom-Json has no -AsHashtable/-Depth/-NoEnumerate/-DateKind, integers decode as Int32 (Int64/Decimal when larger), output is PSCustomObject only, dates arrive as '\/Date(ms)\/' strings from ConvertTo-Json and are auto-converted on input; ConvertTo-Json lacks -EnumsAsStrings/-AsArray/-EscapeHandling, escapes non-ASCII and <>&' as \uXXXX, no depth warning; no OrderedHashtable; System.Text.Json and JsonSchema.Net not present; Newtonsoft not bundled. Conclusion: 5.1 cannot meet the 2020-12 validation MUST without shipping a validator; target PowerShell 7.4+ (declare PowerShellVersion='7.4' in the manifest) and, at most, a degraded 5.1 client mode without schema validation — recommendation: do not support 5.1.

PowerShell 7.4 (net8.0, STJ 8.0, Newtonsoft 13.0.3, JsonSchema.Net 5.2.6 -> 7.0.4 during servicing): ConvertFrom-Json has no -DateKind (date strings always become DateTime); Test-Json has no -Options (no comment/trailing-comma tolerance) and uses OutputFormat.List; no System.Text.Json.Schema.JsonSchemaExporter (STJ 9+); JsonSchema.Net major differs between 7.4.0 and 7.4.13 (API adapter needed).

PowerShell 7.5 (net9.0, STJ 9.0, Newtonsoft 13.0.3, JsonSchema.Net 7.2.3): adds ConvertFrom-Json -DateKind (Default|Local|Utc|Offset|String); Test-Json -Options IgnoreComments/AllowTrailingCommas; STJ 9 adds JsonSchemaExporter, JsonSerializerOptions.Web, JsonElement.DeepEquals, AllowOutOfOrderMetadataProperties.

PowerShell 7.6 (net10.0, STJ 10.0, Newtonsoft 13.0.4, JsonSchema.Net 7.4.0): same cmdlet surface as 7.5 per source at v7.6.0; Test-Json uses OutputFormat.Hierarchical (nested Details walk). Verify any STJ 10 behavioural changes (e.g. new default JsonSerializerOptions, PipeReader support) during implementation.

PowerShell 7.3 boundary (below minimum): -AsHashtable returned a plain Hashtable before 7.3 (unordered); 7.2 stopped serializing ETS properties of DateTime/String; 7.1 introduced the ConvertTo-Json depth warning; 7.0/6.x had different Newtonsoft versions. All below 7.4 are out of support and should be excluded.

MCP revision deltas relevant to JSON handling (changelog items 10-12, Other schema changes): 2026-07-28 loosens inputSchema/outputSchema to any 2020-12 keywords (2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 schema.ts restricted them to {type:'object', properties?, required?}) and structuredContent to any JSON value (previously object-only), adds the $ref-resolution MUST NOT and composition bounds, adds x-mcp-header, removes elicitationId/notifications/elicitation/complete, and fixes schema.json so NumberSchema minimum/maximum/default are numbers not integers. For dual-era support the generator should keep root type:'object' and avoid emitting non-object structuredContent when talking to 2025-11-25 peers, and the elicitation validator must still accept `enumNames` (LegacyTitledEnumSchema, deprecated but present in 2026-07-28 schema.ts).
open_questions: Confirm by experiment on 7.4.x/7.5.x/7.6.x that `[Json.Schema.JsonSchema]` resolves without an explicit Add-Type -Path "$PSHOME/JsonSchema.Net.dll" after Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Utility is loaded, and that loading it explicitly does not create a second copy in a different AssemblyLoadContext.

Verify that a per-options SchemaRegistry.Fetch delegate that throws actually blocks resolution (SchemaRegistry.cs 7.2.3 line 226 uses `Fetch(baseUri) ?? Global.Fetch(baseUri)`, so returning null falls through to Global.Fetch); also verify in 5.2.6 and 7.4.0 whether the fallback and the Fetch signature are the same, and confirm SpecVersion enum member names per version.

Confirm JsonSchema.Net behaviour for $schema-less schemas under SpecVersion.Unspecified (union of all drafts) vs EvaluateAs=Draft202012, especially `items` array form, `definitions` vs `$defs`, and `$ref` sibling keywords; decide whether the SDK injects `$schema` into own schemas (spec: MAY) or relies on EvaluateAs.

Confirm CommentHelpInfo.Parameters key casing (upper-cased vs as-written) and whether FunctionDefinitionAst.GetHelpContent() returns null for help placed above the function keyword vs inside the body.
Measure ConvertFrom-Json vs a PowerShell walker over JsonDocument for 10 KB / 100 KB / 1 MB payloads; determine whether JsonNode pass-through (no materialization) is needed for tool results.

Verify PSObject unwrapping semantics when a PowerShell hashtable containing PSObject-wrapped values is handed to STJ APIs from script (which layers get unwrapped automatically, which do not), and whether `[System.Management.Automation.PSObject]::Base()` is public in all targeted versions.

Decide the Int64-beyond-2^53 policy for generated schemas (type integer with a description note vs type string) and for decoded values (Int64 vs Double vs Decimal fallback for numbers with fractions or exponents); verify how STJ TryGetInt64 treats '1.0' and '1e3' (expected: fails, then Double).

Check Utf8JsonWriter behaviour on Double.NaN/Infinity (throws by default) and the SDK's mapping (reject with error, or null) since JSON cannot represent them; check that decimal values serialize without exponent notation.

Check whether the conformance harness (`wire-schema-valid`) tolerates non-ASCII escaped as \uXXXX and whether it requires `resultType` on every result; not JSON-handling specific but affects the writer's default output.

ConstrainedLanguage / AppLocker scenarios: .NET method calls on STJ/JsonSchema.Net types are blocked in ConstrainedLanguage; decide whether the SDK declares FullLanguage as a hard requirement or ships the pure-PowerShell fallback validator/codec (slower) for those hosts.

Verify ValidateRangeAttribute exposes MinRange/MaxRange as object for ValidateRangeKind-constructed instances (may be null) and how to detect the kind (private field vs public property) across 7.4-7.6.

Verify whether PowerShell class-based attributes (class McpHeaderAttribute : Attribute) are reliably applied to parameters of functions in the same module without `using module`, or whether a hashtable-based override API is the only robust option for x-mcp-header and description metadata.
